resources.string: To find each app\'s cache, Cache Cleaner needs usage access. Android uses it to report storage sizes; the app reads nothing else.
No cache found. Your apps are already clean.

Android lets no app clear another app's cache directly. Cache Cleaner can do it for you by opening each app's Storage page in Settings and pressing Clear cache, as you would.

To do this it uses an Accessibility service. It acts only on Settings screens and only while a cleaning you started is running. It does not read, collect or send anything else.

In the next screen, open Cache Cleaner and turn it on. If Android says the setting is restricted, open App info for Cache Cleaner, tap ⋮, then Allow restricted settings.
Presses Clear cache in Settings for the apps you choose.

Cache Cleaner opens each chosen app\'s Storage page in Settings and presses Clear cache. It acts only on Settings screens and only while a cleaning you started is running. It does not read, collect or send any other content.

Cache Cleaner does not collect, transmit, or share personal data. It has no account, advertising, analytics, tracking, or internet permission. Its only library is Shizuku's open-source API, which talks to the Shizuku app on this device.

Usage access lets Android report each installed app's cache size to Cache Cleaner. The app lists installed apps only to show those sizes.

The Accessibility service is used only to open each chosen app's Storage page in Settings and press Clear cache, while a cleaning you started is running. It does not read or keep any other screen content.

If you install Shizuku and allow Cache Cleaner in it, the app uses it only to run Android's own cache commands.

All of this happens on the device. Your settings and a history of cleanings stay on the device; nothing is sent anywhere.
Could not open the online privacy policy.
Shizuku did not respond. Nothing was cleaned. Check that Shizuku is running.

Clean all uses the Accessibility engine: it opens each app\'s Storage page in Settings and presses Clear cache.\n\nWith Shizuku, Clean all frees every app\'s cache in seconds without opening Settings, and scheduled cleans become possible. Shizuku is a free app that you start once through Wireless debugging or root.
Shizuku is installed but not running. Start it in the Shizuku app through Wireless debugging or root, then come back.
Shizuku is running. Allow Cache Cleaner to use it.
Shizuku permission was denied. Allow Cache Cleaner in the Shizuku app, under Authorized applications.

Shizuku is ready (adb). Clean all frees every app\'s cache at once, in seconds, without opening Settings.\n\nThrough adb, Android does not allow clearing one app at a time, so Clear buttons use the Accessibility engine.
Shizuku is ready (root). Clean all and each Clear button work in the background, app by app, without opening Settings.
You can also long-press an app on the main screen to skip it or include it again.
Shizuku through adb can only clean all apps together. While a skipped app holds cache, Clean all uses the Accessibility engine so that app stays untouched.
Scheduled cleans run in the background, so they need Shizuku. Until Shizuku is ready, each scheduled run is skipped and noted in the history.
Runs in the background through Shizuku and frees every app\'s cache. A run is skipped while a skipped app holds cache.
Runs in the background through Shizuku, app by app, and respects the apps and sizes you skip.
Skipped: a skipped app held cache
